category: HTTP Interface, Web Services, FTP/SFTP, Email & MATLAB Drive
description: The object-oriented matlab.net.http interface (messages, headers, bodies, options, credentials, cookies, streaming content providers and consumers, URIs), base64 utilities, and related connectivity functions (sendmail, ftp, sftp, web, matlabdrive). Complements webread/webwrite/websave/weboptions and matlab.net.http.RequestMessage, which are catalogued elsewhere.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.ResponseMessage
tools.description: Represents the HTTP response returned by RequestMessage.send, with status line, status code, header fields and body. Inspect it to check success, read headers such as Content-Type or Location, and access the converted payload.
tools.usage:
[response, completedRequest, history] = send(request, uri)
response.StatusCode
response.Body.Data
field = response.getFields("Content-Type")

parameters.name: StatusCode
parameters.description: matlab.net.http.StatusCode enumeration, e.g. OK, NotFound.

parameters.name: StatusLine / Header / Body
parameters.description: Status line, HeaderField array and MessageBody.

tools.notes: Bodies are converted by Content-Type (JSON to struct, images to arrays, text to string); use a ContentConsumer for custom handling.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.MessageBody
tools.description: Holds the payload of an HTTP message: MATLAB data (converted according to Content-Type), raw bytes (Payload) or a string. Use it to send JSON, text or binary data in a RequestMessage.
tools.usage:
body = matlab.net.http.MessageBody(data)
body.Data
body.Payload

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: MATLAB data to send (struct/array converted to JSON by default), or uint8 bytes.

parameters.name: ContentType
parameters.description: Media type of the body (read-only, from headers).

tools.notes: For large or streamed payloads use ContentProvider subclasses (FileProvider, JSONProvider, MultipartFormProvider).

tools.name: matlab.net.http.HeaderField
tools.description: Represents a generic HTTP header field (name and value). Arrays of HeaderField objects are passed to RequestMessage to set custom headers like Authorization tokens or Accept types.
tools.usage:
field = matlab.net.http.HeaderField(name, value)
fields = matlab.net.http.HeaderField(name1, value1, ..., nameN, valueN)

parameters.name: name / value
parameters.description: Header name and value as strings.

tools.notes: Specialized subclasses in matlab.net.http.field (ContentTypeField, AuthorizationField, AcceptField, CookieField, ...) validate and parse values. Keep secrets in environment variables, not in code.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.field.ContentTypeField
tools.description: Content-Type header field specifying the media type (and parameters such as charset) of a message body, controlling how MATLAB encodes outgoing data and decodes responses.
tools.usage: field = matlab.net.http.field.ContentTypeField(value)

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Media type string or matlab.net.http.MediaType, e.g. "application/json", "text/csv; charset=UTF-8".

tools.notes: MediaType objects parse type, subtype and parameters.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.field.AuthorizationField
tools.description: Authorization (or Proxy-Authorization) header field carrying credentials such as Bearer tokens or Basic auth, for APIs that require explicit authorization headers.
tools.usage: field = matlab.net.http.field.AuthorizationField("Authorization", value)

parameters.name: value
parameters.description: Credentials string, e.g. "Bearer <token>", or an AuthInfo object.

tools.notes: For Basic/Digest/NTLM authentication prefer matlab.net.http.Credentials in HTTPOptions, which answers server challenges automatically.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.RequestMethod
tools.description: Enumeration of HTTP request methods (GET, POST, PUT, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, CONNECT) used to construct RequestMessage objects.
tools.usage:
method = matlab.net.http.RequestMethod.GET
request = matlab.net.http.RequestMessage(method)

parameters.name: members
parameters.description: GET, PUT, POST, DELETE, PATCH, HEAD, OPTIONS, TRACE, CONNECT.

tools.notes: Strings such as "POST" are accepted wherever a RequestMethod is expected.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.StatusCode
tools.description: Enumeration of HTTP status codes (OK = 200, Created = 201, NotFound = 404, ...) with helper methods to get the status class and reason phrase, used to test responses robustly.
tools.usage:
code = response.StatusCode
cls = getClass(code)
phrase = getReasonPhrase(code)

parameters.name: members
parameters.description: Named codes such as OK, Created, NoContent, MovedPermanently, BadRequest, Unauthorized, Forbidden, NotFound, InternalServerError.

tools.notes: Unlike webread, send does not throw on 4xx/5xx; check StatusCode yourself.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.HTTPOptions
tools.description: Options controlling HTTP message exchange: timeouts, redirects, credentials, proxy, certificate verification, automatic content conversion, progress monitoring and buffering.
tools.usage:
options = matlab.net.http.HTTPOptions(Name=Value)
response = send(request, uri, options)

parameters.name: ConnectTimeout / ResponseTimeout
parameters.description: Timeouts in seconds.

parameters.name: MaxRedirects
parameters.description: Number of redirects to follow (default 20).

parameters.name: Credentials
parameters.description: matlab.net.http.Credentials objects for authentication challenges.

parameters.name: UseProxy / ProxyURI / CertificateFilename / VerifyServerName
parameters.description: Proxy and TLS settings.

parameters.name: ConvertResponse / ProgressMonitorFcn / UseProgressMonitor
parameters.description: Payload conversion and progress reporting.

tools.notes: Setting CertificateFilename to "" disables server certificate verification; avoid this outside testing.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.Credentials
tools.description: Holds user name/password credentials (or a GetCredentialsFcn callback) that HTTPOptions uses to answer Basic, Digest or NTLM authentication challenges for specified scopes and realms.
tools.usage: creds = matlab.net.http.Credentials(Name=Value)

parameters.name: Username / Password
parameters.description: Account credentials.

parameters.name: Scope / Realm
parameters.description: URIs and realms where the credentials apply.

parameters.name: Scheme
parameters.description: Allowed authentication schemes (Basic, Digest, NTLM).

parameters.name: GetCredentialsFcn
parameters.description: Callback returning credentials on demand (avoid storing passwords).

tools.notes: Credentials are only sent to URIs within Scope. Avoid hard-coding secrets in scripts.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.Cookie
tools.description: Represents an HTTP cookie received from a server via Set-Cookie. Collect cookies from a response (CookieInfo) and send them back with a CookieField to maintain sessions.
tools.usage:
cookieInfos = matlab.net.http.CookieInfo.collectFromLog(history)
cookies = [cookieInfos.Cookie]
field = matlab.net.http.field.CookieField(cookies)

parameters.name: Name / Value
parameters.description: Cookie name and value.

parameters.name: CookieInfo
parameters.description: Wrapper with domain, path, expiry and secure flags.

tools.notes: MATLAB does not maintain a cookie jar automatically across send calls.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.ProgressMonitor
tools.description: Abstract class for monitoring the progress of HTTP transfers; implement a subclass (e.g. updating a waitbar) and supply it via HTTPOptions ProgressMonitorFcn for large uploads or downloads.
tools.usage:
classdef MyMonitor < matlab.net.http.ProgressMonitor
    methods
        function done(obj) ... end
        function set.Value(obj, value) ... end
    end
end
opts = matlab.net.http.HTTPOptions(ProgressMonitorFcn=@MyMonitor, UseProgressMonitor=true)

parameters.name: Value / Max / Direction
parameters.description: Bytes transferred, total bytes and transfer direction.

parameters.name: done
parameters.description: Method called when the transfer completes.

tools.notes: Progress updates occur roughly every second; avoid heavy work in the setter.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.HTTPException
tools.description: Exception thrown by send when a network or protocol error prevents completing the exchange (not for HTTP error status codes). Its History property contains the log records, including the request actually sent.
tools.usage:
try
    resp = send(req, uri);
catch ME
    if isa(ME, "matlab.net.http.HTTPException")
        ME.History
    end
end

parameters.name: History
parameters.description: Array of matlab.net.http.LogRecord for diagnostics.

parameters.name: URI / Request
parameters.description: Target URI and request message.

tools.example:
try
    resp = send(matlab.net.http.RequestMessage("GET"), "https://no-such-host.invalid");
catch ME
    disp(ME.message)
end
tools.notes: LogRecord objects include raw request/response headers and timing (Disposition).

tools.name: matlab.net.http.io.MultipartFormProvider
tools.description: Content provider that sends multipart/form-data bodies, e.g. to upload files together with form fields to a web API, streaming file contents without loading them fully into memory.
tools.usage: provider = matlab.net.http.io.MultipartFormProvider(name1, part1, ..., nameN, partN)

parameters.name: name / part
parameters.description: Form field names and their contents: strings, numbers, or other providers such as FileProvider.

tools.notes: Other providers: FileProvider (single file), FormProvider (application/x-www-form-urlencoded), JSONProvider, StringProvider, ImageProvider, MultipartProvider.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.io.FileProvider
tools.description: Content provider that streams one or more files as the body of a request, setting Content-Type from the file extension; used for uploads with PUT/POST.
tools.usage: provider = matlab.net.http.io.FileProvider(filenames)

parameters.name: filenames
parameters.description: File path or string array of paths (multiple files become multipart/mixed).

tools.notes: Streaming avoids memory spikes for large files.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.io.FormProvider
tools.description: Content provider that sends HTML form data in application/x-www-form-urlencoded format from name/value pairs or QueryParameter objects.
tools.usage:
provider = matlab.net.http.io.FormProvider(name1, value1, ..., nameN, valueN)
provider = matlab.net.http.io.FormProvider(queryParameters)

parameters.name: name / value
parameters.description: Form fields.

tools.notes: Values are URL-encoded automatically.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.io.JSONProvider
tools.description: Content provider that encodes MATLAB data as JSON (using jsonencode) and streams it as the request body with Content-Type application/json.
tools.usage:
provider = matlab.net.http.io.JSONProvider(data)
provider = matlab.net.http.io.JSONProvider(data, jsonencodeArgs)

parameters.name: data
parameters.description: Struct, table, array or other jsonencode-compatible data.

parameters.name: jsonencodeArgs
parameters.description: Extra arguments passed to jsonencode (e.g. PrettyPrint).

tools.notes: Equivalent to MessageBody with JSON conversion but streams the content.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.io.FileConsumer
tools.description: Content consumer that streams a response body directly to a file (optionally choosing the name from Content-Disposition), for downloading large files without holding them in memory.
tools.usage:
consumer = matlab.net.http.io.FileConsumer
consumer = matlab.net.http.io.FileConsumer(filename)
response = send(request, uri, options, consumer)

parameters.name: filename
parameters.description: Target file or folder; default chosen from the response.

parameters.name: AllowExisting
parameters.description: Overwrite existing files.

tools.notes: websave is the simpler function-based alternative for single downloads.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.io.JSONConsumer
tools.description: Content consumer that converts a JSON response payload into MATLAB data using jsondecode, useful when you need custom decoding options or streaming JSON handling.
tools.usage:
consumer = matlab.net.http.io.JSONConsumer
consumer = matlab.net.http.io.JSONConsumer(jsondecodeArgs)
response = send(request, uri, options, consumer)

parameters.name: jsondecodeArgs
parameters.description: Arguments passed to jsondecode (e.g. "makeValidName", false).

tools.notes: Other consumers: StringConsumer, ImageConsumer, BinaryConsumer, MultipartConsumer, GenericConsumer; subclass ContentConsumer for streaming processing.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.io.ContentConsumer
tools.description: Base class for custom streaming consumers of HTTP response payloads. Override putData to process chunks as they arrive, e.g. parsing server-sent events or progressively writing records.
tools.usage:
classdef MyConsumer < matlab.net.http.io.ContentConsumer
    methods
        function [len, stop] = putData(obj, data) ... end
    end
end

parameters.name: putData(obj, data)
parameters.description: Called with uint8 chunks; empty data signals end of stream. Return stop=true to abort.

parameters.name: Response / Header / ContentType
parameters.description: Context available to the consumer.

tools.notes: Delegate to other consumers via delegateTo for multipart content.

tools.name: matlab.net.URI
tools.description: Represents and builds uniform resource identifiers, handling scheme, host, port, path segments and query parameters with correct percent-encoding.
tools.usage:
uri = matlab.net.URI(uriString)
uri = matlab.net.URI(uriString, queryParameters)
uri = matlab.net.URI(uriString, name1, value1, ...)

parameters.name: Scheme / Host / Port / Path / Query / Fragment
parameters.description: URI components (settable properties).

tools.notes: Use EncodedURI for the fully encoded string. QueryParameter and ArrayFormat control array encoding in queries.

tools.name: matlab.net.QueryParameter
tools.description: Represents query parameters of a URI (name/value pairs), with control over how array values are formatted (repeating, comma-separated, JSON, PHP style).
tools.usage:
qp = matlab.net.QueryParameter(name1, value1, ..., nameN, valueN)
qp = matlab.net.QueryParameter(struct)
qp = matlab.net.QueryParameter(___, format)

parameters.name: format
parameters.description: matlab.net.ArrayFormat: csv, json, php or repeating.

tools.notes: Also used by FormProvider to build form bodies.

tools.name: matlab.net.base64encode
tools.description: Encodes a byte vector or string as a Base64 string (RFC 4648), e.g. for embedding binary data in JSON or building Basic authentication headers.
tools.usage: b64 = matlab.net.base64encode(V)

parameters.name: V
parameters.description: uint8 vector, character vector or string (text is encoded as UTF-8).

tools.notes: matlab.net.base64decode is the inverse and returns uint8.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.field.AcceptField
tools.description: Accept header field listing the media types the client is willing to receive, optionally with quality (q) weights, so servers that support content negotiation return JSON, XML, CSV or images as requested.
tools.usage: field = matlab.net.http.field.AcceptField(mediaTypes)

parameters.name: mediaTypes
parameters.description: String array or matlab.net.http.MediaType array, e.g. ["application/json" "text/csv;q=0.5"].

tools.notes: If no Accept field is supplied, MATLAB sends a default that accepts common types.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.MediaType
tools.description: Represents an Internet media type (type/subtype plus parameters such as charset or q) used in Content-Type and Accept header fields, with parsing and comparison helpers.
tools.usage:
mt = matlab.net.http.MediaType(typeString)
mt = matlab.net.http.MediaType(typeString, paramName1, paramValue1, ...)

parameters.name: Type / Subtype / MediaInfo / Weight
parameters.description: Components of the media type.

tools.notes: Use with ContentTypeField and AcceptField.

tools.name: matlab.net.http.LogRecord
tools.description: Record of one HTTP request/response exchange returned in the history output of send (and in HTTPException.History), containing the actual request and response messages, URI, timing and disposition; essential for debugging redirects and authentication.
tools.usage:
[response, completedRequest, history] = send(request, uri)
history(k).Request
history(k).Response
show(history)

parameters.name: URI / Request / Response
parameters.description: Exchange details for each hop (including redirects and auth retries).

parameters.name: RequestTime / ResponseTime / Disposition
parameters.description: Timing and outcome (matlab.net.http.Disposition).

tools.notes: Pass SavePayload=true in HTTPOptions to keep raw payloads in the log.

tools.name: sendmail
tools.description: Sends an email with optional attachments through an SMTP server configured with setpref (server, sender address, authentication and TLS settings via Java properties).
tools.usage:
sendmail(recipients, subject)
sendmail(recipients, subject, message)
sendmail(recipients, subject, message, attachments)

parameters.name: recipients
parameters.description: Email address or string array/cell array of addresses.

parameters.name: message
parameters.description: Body text; cell arrays produce multiple lines.

parameters.name: attachments
parameters.description: File path(s) to attach.

tools.notes: Authenticated servers need SMTP_Username/SMTP_Password preferences and Java mail properties (mail.smtp.auth, mail.smtp.starttls.enable); avoid storing passwords in scripts.

tools.name: ftp
tools.description: Opens a connection to an FTP server and returns an object for listing, navigating, uploading (mput) and downloading (mget) files, optionally with TLS.
tools.usage:
f = ftp(host)
f = ftp(host, username, password)
f = ftp(___, Name=Value)

parameters.name: host
parameters.description: Server name, optionally with port ("ftp.example.com:21").

parameters.name: TLSMode / Mode / LocalDataConnectionMethod
parameters.description: "none", "strict" or "opportunistic" TLS; ASCII/binary mode; passive/active.

tools.notes: Prefer sftp (SSH File Transfer Protocol) for secure transfers. Methods: dir, cd, mget, mput, rename, delete, mkdir, rmdir, close.

tools.name: sftp
tools.description: Opens an SFTP (SSH File Transfer Protocol) connection to a server for secure file listing, upload (mput) and download (mget), using password or public-key authentication.
tools.usage:
s = sftp(host, username)
s = sftp(host, username, Name=Value)

parameters.name: host / username
parameters.description: Server (optionally with :port) and account name.

parameters.name: Password / PublicKeyFile / PrivateKeyFile
parameters.description: Authentication options.

parameters.name: DatetimeType / ServerLocale
parameters.description: Directory listing parsing options.

tools.notes: Shares the mget/mput/dir/cd interface of ftp objects.

tools.name: web
tools.description: Opens a URL or HTML file in the MATLAB web browser or the system browser; commonly used to display generated HTML reports or documentation pages.
tools.usage:
web(url)
web(url, "-new")
web(url, "-browser")
[stat, h] = web(___)

parameters.name: url
parameters.description: Web address or local HTML file path.

parameters.name: -new / -notoolbar / -noaddressbox / -browser
parameters.description: Window and browser options (-browser uses the system browser).

tools.notes: Not available in matlab -batch sessions without a display. Use webread to fetch content programmatically instead.

tools.name: matlabdrive
tools.description: Returns the path of the local folder synchronized with MATLAB Drive (or the MATLAB Drive root in MATLAB Online), enabling portable file paths that work both on the desktop and online.
tools.usage: folder = matlabdrive
tools.notes: On desktop systems MATLAB Drive Connector must be installed; otherwise matlabdrive errors. Files in MATLAB Drive can be shared with others from MATLAB Online.
